title: Heralded Free-Electron Writing of the Most Subradiant State in an Atomic Array
authors: Tong Shen, Zhexin Zhao, Meng Xiao
abstract: The most subradiant eigenstate of a finite subwavelength atomic chain in free space, protected by strongly suppressed radiative decay, offers a powerful resource for photon storage, quantum sensing, and many-body quantum optics. Yet its optical preparation is hindered by the simultaneous need to match a wave vector outside the light cone and a nonuniform envelope. Here, we show that a free electron can overcome these constraints: its velocity sets the imprinted wave vector, while the trajectory of the diffracting wave packet shapes the excitation envelope. This simultaneous momentum and envelope matching enables heralded preparation with near-unity conditional fidelity ($F>99.5\%$) even in a deeply subwavelength regime that is difficult to access with propagating free-space photons. We further show that a path-superposed free electron can excite an antisymmetric state in two closely spaced parallel chains, whose interchain destructive interference yields stronger subradiance than a single chain with the same total number of atoms. These results establish free electrons as quantum writers for collective excitations that are difficult to access with propagating optical fields.
summary: The paper demonstrates that free electrons can act as 'quantum writers' to prepare highly subradiant collective excitations in atomic chains. By leveraging the electron's momentum and trajectory, they overcome fundamental limitations faced by optical preparation methods. This technique achieves near-perfect fidelity even in deeply subwavelength regimes, opening new avenues for quantum memory and sensing.
main_problem: The primary challenge is optically preparing the most subradiant eigenstate in a deeply subwavelength atomic chain because this state requires matching both an out-of-cone wave vector and a nonuniform spatial envelope.
main_result: A free electron passing through the array can overcome these constraints, achieving near-unity conditional fidelity ($F>99.5\%$) even at deep subwavelength spacings. Furthermore, path superposition in two chains yields stronger subradiance than single chains.
method: The authors model the interaction using a scattering operator and utilize the free electron's velocity to set momentum while its trajectory shapes the excitation envelope for heralded preparation via EELS detection.
model_or_system: The system is an ordered 1D array (chain) of two-level atoms. The physics involves collective eigenmodes described by a non-Hermitian Hamiltonian, and the interaction is treated perturbatively using electron scattering theory.
key_observables: Conditional fidelity ($F$), minimum decay rate ($\gamma_{	ext{min}}$), excitation probability ($P_{	ext{exc}}$), and the ratio of decay rates in two chains ($\Gamma(N)_{anti} / \gamma(N/2)_{min}$).
important_parameters: Deeply subwavelength spacing ($a = \lambda_0/20$), near-unity fidelity ($F > 99.5\%$), and the free electron's velocity ($v_0$).
main_assumptions: Approximations include Born–Markov, non-recoil for the electron, and using Gaussian beam profiles with parabolic trajectories induced by DC electric fields.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the comparison between photon and free-electron dispersion relations, showing how $\mathbf{q} = \omega_0/v_0$ enables access to subradiant modes. Later figures map out fidelity landscapes based on beam waist and trajectory curvature for optimized preparation.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from establishing the fundamental difficulty of state preparation in deep subwavelength regimes, introducing the free-electron writing mechanism using momentum/envelope matching, extending this protocol to two parallel chains via path superposition, and finally analyzing robustness against energy spread.
why_interesting: This work provides a concrete, high-fidelity method for engineering collective quantum states (superradiance/subradiance) that are otherwise inaccessible with standard propagating light fields, which is crucial for advanced quantum sensing and memory applications in AMO physics.

FIG. 2. Free-electron heralding protocol and straight- trajectory benchmark. (a) Schematic of the EELS-based setup. A quasi-monochromatic electron is emitted from an electron gun, focused onto the atomic chain by an electro- magnetic lens, and analyzed after the interaction by EELS. (b) Electron energy spectrum before and after the interaction. (c) Conditional fidelity F for preparing the most subradiant state using a diffraction-free, well-focused straight electron trajectory, illustrated in the inset. The fidelity approaches the 8/π2 ≈81% limit for large N.

FIG. 3. (a) Schematic of a diffracting Gaussian electron wave packet steered by a vertical DC electric field EDC. The dashed line marks the center of the electron wave packet, while the yellow shaded region denotes rmid(z)±w(z). The parameters correspond to the optimal point marked by the red stars in (b) and (c). Other parameters are N = 21, λ0 = 780 nm, a/λ0 = 1/20, n = 1 (with electron velocity v0 = c/30), and r0 = 5 nm. (b, c) Conditional fidelity (b) and excitation probability (c) as functions of the beam waist w0 and trajectory curvature α. The red star indicates the maximum-fidelity point, with Fmax = 99.55% and Pexc = 2.97 × 10−4.

FIG. 4. (a) Scheme for heralding an antisymmetric excita- tion in two parallel atomic chains. A path-superposed elec- tron interacts with the two chains and is recombined before EELS detection. The inset defines the interchain spacing d. (b) Decay rate Γ(N) anti/γ0 of the antisymmetric state as a func- tion of the interchain spacing d for several total atom numbers N. All other unspecified parameters are the same as those in Fig. 3. The horizontal dashed lines indicate γ(50) min and γ(100) min for single chains, serving as references for the two-chain decay suppression. The vertical dashed line marks d = 98 nm, used as a representative interchain spacing for this comparison.

FIG. 1. Decomposition of the most subradiant eigenstate in a finite atomic chain. Left: dominant staggered component cjeiπzj/a of the numerically obtained most subradiant eigenstate for N = 21 and a = λ0/3, showing the alternating sign structure and the nonuniform envelope. Right: residual phase profile δφj/π after removing the dominant staggered phase. The residual phase is small compared with the leading π phase difference between neighboring atoms, justifying its neglect in the qualitative phase-matching discussion. In the numerical fidelity calculations, the exact eigenstate including this residual phase profile is used as the target state.
